prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies transformer/feeder bays and distribution circuits. Automation covers bay control, station coordination, and external interfaces; primary equipment/protection/wiring follow approved designs/limits.

Bay Automation Controller (Juniper) sequences bays, evaluates status/permissives, produces Bay Status Digest, and requests breaker operations only under permitted modes/permissives. North Bay Controller and South Bay Controller automate respective portions. Breaker Control Unit executes authorized operations; local electrical/mechanical interlocks and equipment logic remain authoritative. Local-selected equipment prioritizes local control; remote commands require station authority, bay selection, interlocking, availability, configured permissions, and operating procedures.

Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem) detects faults/trips within its protection zone; produces Relay Diagnostic Note for self-monitoring conditions requiring engineering attention. Protection trips remain independent of routine control; control failure must not inhibit clearing. Supervisory functions do not perform protection.

Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing) consolidates station/bay indications, operating conditions, and communications quality without replacing local indications; produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip. Station Gateway carries authorized supervisory communications between station functions and remote operations interfaces. Visibility depends on communications/status quality; interruptions cause stale/unavailable displays; operators must verify currency after recovery.

Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin) acquires supported satellite references and distributes time over the configured network; produces Clock Drift Snapshot at configured offset-reporting condition. Receiving equipment applies time for consistent timestamps; timestamp accuracy does not validate measurements/protection decisions. Reference loss invokes device-specific, potentially degrading holdover; quality indications distinguish synchronized/degraded/unavailable timing.

Station DC System powers automation/protection within capacity; power loss may interrupt visibility/time distribution until supplies recover. Sequence Event Archive retains events. Engineering Workstation supports controlled configuration/maintenance; Maintenance Remote Terminal permits approved maintenance without superseding local authority.

Control Room Operator assesses displays, coordinates operations, verifies states. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur) maintains settings/evaluates performance through approved changes. Substation Field Crew follows switching instructions/clearances. Substation Supervisor oversees supervisory use/escalates unresolved availability concerns.

New part:
S052: The Feeder Protection Relay provides local protection for its assigned feeder and operates independently of supervisory control availability.
S053: Its approved setting group defines the pickup levels, time delays, and logic required for the feeder protection scheme.
S054: The Protection Relay Engineer develops setting changes against the approved protection study and the current equipment data.
S055: The Protection Relay Engineer documents the engineering basis and expected operational effect for each proposed change.
S056: Engineering Workstation maintains the working configuration under revision control.
S057: Engineering Workstation produces the Settings Review Receipt after a settings review is completed.
S058: Each proposed change receives a unique revision identifier before review begins.
S059: The Protection Relay Engineer verifies that proposed values agree with the approved coordination objectives.
S060: A second qualified reviewer independently checks calculations, logic changes, and device applicability.
S061: The review confirms that the proposed configuration is complete, internally consistent, and suitable for the intended feeder.
S062: Coordination checks consider upstream and downstream protection behavior across the expected operating range.
S063: Protection settings are not approved solely on the basis of copied values from another installation.
S064: Engineering Workstation retains the approved configuration and its revision history for controlled access.
S065: Configuration access is limited to personnel with assigned engineering responsibilities.
S066: The Protection Relay Engineer records the approval status before any setting change is released for implementation.
S067: Before deployment, the approved configuration is checked against the intended device model and firmware version.
S068: A controlled outage or other approved work window is required when implementation could affect feeder protection.
S069: The Substation Field Crew follows the authorized work instructions during device access and setting transfer.
S070: After installation, the implemented values are compared with the approved configuration.
S071: The Feeder Protection Relay is functionally checked to confirm the intended protection behavior after a change.
S072: Any discrepancy stops release of the configuration until its cause is resolved and reviewed.
S073: The Substation Supervisor ensures that engineering changes follow the established authorization and operational control process.
S074: The Substation Field Crew is known operationally as Cinder during field activities.
S075: Cinder performs inspections, maintenance, and switching support within the boundaries of approved work.
S076: Field access begins only after the required work authorization and site entry controls are confirmed.
S077: The Control Room Operator coordinates operational access with the Switching Desk Coordinator before work that could affect energized equipment.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
